questions.question:
From the alternatives given below, choose the correct meaning of the idiom
'eat an elephant one bite at a time'.

options.text: To have seen or experienced as much as one can endure
To accomplish a large goal by doing smaller, cumulative tasks

questions.question: Which of the following words is the closest synonym of the word "diversity"?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Variety**.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **'diversity'** refers to the state of being diverse; it indicates a range of different things or the inclusion of many different elements. (विविधता)
 
 
• **Example:** The biological **diversity** of the rainforest is truly breathtaking.
 
 
 
• **'Variety'** refers to the quality or state of being different or diverse, and it is used to describe a collection of different things of the same general type. It is the closest synonym to diversity. (विभिन्नता)
 
 
• **Example:** The menu offers a wide **variety** of seafood dishes.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the closest synonym of **'diversity'** is **'variety'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is- **Variety**.

**Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Sameness** (समानता): The quality of being the same; a lack of variety or change.
 
 
• **Example:** The **sameness** of the daily routine started to become tiring.
 
 
 
• **Uniformity** (एकरूपता): The quality or state of being uniform; consistency or staying the same in all cases and at all times.
 
 
• **Example:** The factory maintains a high level of **uniformity** in its production process.
 
 
 
• **Simplicity** (सादगी): The quality or condition of being easy to understand or do; the state of being plain or uncomplicated.
 
 
• **Example:** I admire the **simplicity** and elegance of her writing style.

questions.question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into Passive Voice?
Some people still think that the Earth is flat!

options.text: The Earth is still thought to be flat by some people!
It was thought by some people still that the Earth is flat.
Earth is thought flat by some people still!
The Earth is thought of as being flat by some people.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Earth is still thought to be flat by some people!**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence is in the **Active Voice** following the structure: **Subject** (Some people) + **Verb** (think) + **Noun Clause** (that the Earth is flat).
 
• When converting sentences with **Reporting Verbs** (like think, believe, say, or claim) into the **Passive Voice**, two structures are commonly used: the **Impersonal Passive** (starting with 'It is...') or the **Personal Passive** (starting with the subject of the clause).
 
• In the **Personal Passive** construction, the subject of the subordinate clause (**The Earth**) becomes the subject of the passive sentence. The main verb (**think**), which is in the **Present Indefinite Tense**, is changed to **is thought**. Hence, the structure becomes **Subject + is/am/are + Past Participle + to-infinitive**.
 
• The verb in the subordinate clause (**is**) is replaced by its **Infinitive** form (**to be**) to maintain grammatical continuity. The adverb **still** is placed before the past participle to retain the original meaning and emphasis.
 
• Finally, the original subject (**Some people**) is introduced using the preposition **by**. Therefore, the transformation yields: **The Earth is still thought to be flat by some people!**

 **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Impersonal Passive** version of this sentence would be: **It is still thought by some people that the Earth is flat!** However, this was not provided among the correct options.
 
• **Verbs of Perception and Cognition:**
 
 
• Verbs like **consider**, **know**, **report**, and **understand** follow this same rule of **Passive Transformation**.
 
• If the action in the subordinate clause happened before the thinking, a **Perfect Infinitive** (to have been) would be used instead of a **Simple Infinitive** (to be).
 
• **Tense Consistency:** In option 2, the use of **was thought** is incorrect because the original sentence is in the **Present Tense**. Passive voice must always preserve the **Tense** of the active verb.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into Passive Voice?
They allege that the man is a cheat.

options.text: The man was alleged to be a cheat.
The man was a cheat they alleged.
It is alleged that the man is a cheat.
The man is alleged to have cheated.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It is alleged that the man is a cheat.**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence **They allege that the man is a cheat** follows a structure where the **subject** is the indefinite pronoun **They**, followed by a **reporting verb** (allege), and a **noun clause** (that the man is a cheat) acting as the **direct object**.
 
• To convert sentences with a **that-clause** into the **passive voice**, the **impersonal passive** construction is commonly used, which begins with the formal introductory subject **It**.
 
• The **reporting verb** in the active sentence, **allege**, is in the **Simple Present Tense**. In the **passive voice**, this tense is formed using **is/am/are + past participle (V3)**. Since **It** is a **third-person singular** subject, the auxiliary verb **is** is used followed by **alleged**.
 
• The **subordinate noun clause** (that the man is a cheat) remains in its original form and is placed after the **passive reporting verb**.
 
• This transformation shifts the emphasis from the **anonymous subject** (They) to the **statement of allegation** itself, making the tone more **formal** and **objective**.

 **Additional Information__**

 
• **Reporting Verbs and Passive Structures**:
 
 
• Verbs such as **say**, **believe**, **think**, **claim**, and **report** follow this same pattern when the **active subject** is **general** or **unknown**.
 
• **Tense Mismatch**: The options **The man was alleged to be a cheat** and **The man was a cheat they alleged** are incorrect because they use the **Past Tense** (was), whereas the original sentence is in the **Present Tense**.
 
• **Infinitive Conversion**: While a **personal passive** like **The man is alleged to be a cheat** is a valid alternative, the **impersonal passive** starting with **It** is the most direct conversion for the provided options.
 
• **Meaning Shift**: The option **The man is alleged to have cheated** uses a **perfect infinitive**, which suggests a completed past action rather than the current **stative identity** of being a **cheat** mentioned in the original text.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
Select the correct alternative to fill in the blank with the correct preposition in the following sentence.

There had been a large number of oranges the tree last year.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**in**'. **__Key Points__** __ 
• The preposition '**in**' is used to describe something located within the area or volume of a three-dimensional space, such as the canopy, branches, and leaves of a tree. 
• Since fruits like oranges grow and hang nestled inside the branches and foliage of a tree, the phrase '**in the tree**' is grammatically correct and suitable in this context. Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**. **Complete Sentence:** *'There had been a large number of oranges **in**__ the tree last year.'* **__Additional Information__** 
• **Option 1: 'at'** is incorrect because it is used to indicate a specific point or location, not containment. 
• **Option 2: 'on'** usually refers to being on the surface of something, but 'in the tree' is the correct choice here to refer to the oranges within the tree's branches. 
• **Option 4: 'with'** is incorrect as it indicates accompaniment or using an instrument. </ul

questions.question:
A part of the following sentence is underlined. Choose the option which can replace the underlined part to improve the sentence. In case Options A, B and C are not found suitable, choose Option D: "No Improvement Required."

The police__ has arrested the thief along with__ his accomplices yesterday.

options.text: have arrested the thief along with
had arrested the thief along with

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence includes the specific time marker **yesterday**, which indicates a completed action in the past.
 
• When a sentence contains a definite point of time in the past (such as **yesterday**, **last night**, or **two days ago**), the **Simple Past Tense** must be used instead of the **Present Perfect Tense**.
 
• The phrase **has arrested** is in the **Present Perfect Tense**, which is grammatically incorrect when paired with a specific past time reference.
 
• The correct verb form to replace it is **arrested**, which is the **Simple Past** form.

Therefore, the correct answer is **arrested the thief along with**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *'The police **arrested the thief along with** his accomplices yesterday.'*

 

**Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1 ('have arrested the thief along with'):** This uses the **Present Perfect Tense** (plural), which is still incorrect because of the specific time reference **yesterday**.
 
• **Option 2 ('had arrested the thief along with'):** This uses the **Past Perfect Tense**. The **Past Perfect** is generally used to describe an action that happened before another action in the past, rather than a single event with a specific time stamp like **yesterday**.
 
• **Option 4 ('No improvement required'):** This is incorrect because the original sentence uses the **Present Perfect Tense** with a past time marker, violating standard grammar rules.
 
• Note: While 'police' is a collective noun usually treated as plural (taking 'have' or 'are'), the primary grammatical error here is the **tense** mismatch with the word **yesterday**.
</ul

questions.question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1. While he still gazed upward into the deep arch of the firmament and had lifted his hands to pray, a cloud, though no wind was stirring, hurried across the zenith and hid the brightening stars.

A. The blue sky was still visible, except directly overhead, where this black mass of cloud was sweeping swiftly northward.

B. The next moment, so indistinct were the sounds, he doubted whether he had heard aught but the murmur of the old forest, whispering without a wind.

C. Once the listener fancied that he could distinguish the accents of townspeople of his own, men and women, both pious and ungodly, many of whom he had met at the communion table and had seen others rioting at the tavern.

D. Aloft in the air, as if from the depths of the cloud, came a confused and doubtful sound of voices.

S2. Then came a stronger swell of those familiar tones, heard daily in the sunshine at Salem village, but never until now from a cloud of night
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**__Key Points__**

 
• The paragraph describes a supernatural or eerie experience involving a **cloud** and **mysterious voices** heard at night.
 
• **Sentence A follows S1**: S1 introduces a **cloud** hurrying across the zenith. **Sentence A** continues this visual description by identifying the cloud as a **black mass** sweeping northward while noting that the rest of the **blue sky** was still visible.
 
• **Sentence D follows A**: After establishing the cloud's position directly overhead, **Sentence D** introduces a new sensory element—a **confused and doubtful sound of voices** coming from the depths of that very cloud.
 
• **Sentence C follows D**: This sentence provides more detail about the **voices** mentioned in D. The listener begins to recognize the **accents of townspeople**, including both **pious** individuals and those seen at the **tavern**.
 
• **Sentence B follows C**: After the specific identification in C, the listener experiences a moment of **doubt**. **Sentence B** explains that the sounds became so indistinct that he wondered if it was just the **murmur of the old forest**.
 
• **S2 completes the sequence**: The doubt in B is resolved in **S2**, where a **stronger swell** of those familiar tones from **Salem village** is heard, confirming that the voices were real.
 
• The correct logical sequence is **ADCB**.

 

**Coherent paragraph after rearrangement**:

'While he still gazed upward into the deep arch of the firmament and had lifted his hands to pray, a cloud, though no wind was stirring, hurried across the zenith and hid the brightening stars. The blue sky was still visible, except directly overhead, where this black mass of cloud was sweeping swiftly northward. Aloft in the air, as if from the depths of the cloud, came a confused and doubtful sound of voices. Once the listener fancied that he could distinguish the accents of townspeople of his own, men and women, both pious and ungodly, many of whom he had met at the communion table and had seen others rioting at the tavern. The next moment, so indistinct were the sounds, he doubted whether he had heard aught but the murmur of the old forest, whispering without a wind. Then came a stronger swell of those familiar tones, heard daily in the sunshine at Salem village, but never until now from a cloud of night.'

 

Therefore, the correct sequence is **ADCB**.

questions.question:
A part of the following sentence is underlined. Choose the option that can replace the underlined part to improve the sentence. If you feel Options A, B, or C do not improve the sentence, then choose Option D: "No improvement required."

The government needs to __address environmental concerns, provide financial support to affected communities, and increase awareness__ among the general public.

options.text: address environmental concerns, providing financial support, and increase awareness
addressing environmental concerns, provide financial support, and increase awareness
address environmental concerns, provide financial support, and increasing awareness

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**No improvement required**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence follows the grammatical rule of **Parallelism**, which dictates that items in a series or list must share the same **grammatical structure** to ensure clarity and balance.
 
• In this sentence, the phrase **needs to** functions as the lead-in to a series of three **infinitive actions**. The **to-infinitive** marker (to) applies to all subsequent verbs in the list: **address**, **provide**, and **increase**.
 
• The first verb, **address**, is in its **base form**. To maintain consistency, every subsequent verb in the list must also remain in the base form.
 
• The second verb, **provide**, correctly maintains this **base form**, ensuring it is parallel with 'address'.
 
• The third verb, **increase**, similarly follows the **base form** structure, effectively completing the parallel sequence connected by the coordinating conjunction **and**.
 
• Since all three components—**address**, **provide**, and **increase**—are in the same grammatical form, the sentence is technically and stylistically correct as written.

 **Additional Information__**

 
• **Parallel Structure**:
 
 
• This concept is essential in **formal writing** and **competitive exams** to avoid **faulty parallelism**, which occurs when items in a series have different grammatical forms.
 
• When using the **infinitive** ('to' + verb) in a list, you can either repeat the 'to' before every verb (e.g., to address, to provide, and to increase) or use it only once before the first verb, provided all subsequent verbs are in the **base form**.
 
 
 
• **Incorrect Option Analysis**:
 
 
• **Option 1**: Uses the **present participle** (providing), which breaks the flow established by the base verbs 'address' and 'increase'.
 
• **Option 2**: Starts with the **gerund/participle** (addressing), which does not logically follow the infinitive marker 'to' in this context.
 
• **Option 3**: Concludes with **increasing**, creating an **asymmetrical list** because the first two verbs are in the base form while the third is not.

questions.question:
A part of the following sentence is underlined. Choose the option that can replace the underlined part to improve the sentence. If you feel Options A, B, or C do not improve the sentence, then choose Option D: "No improvement required."

Climbing Mount Everest is not small feat; it requires months of preparation, physical endurance, and mental strength.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**is no small feat**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The expression **no small feat** is a widely used **idiomatic phrase** in the English language which signifies that an achievement is **significant**, **difficult**, or requires **extraordinary effort**.
 
• In the given sentence, the original phrase **is not small feat** is grammatically incorrect because the **singular countable noun** **feat** requires an article (like **a**) or a determiner (like **no**) to function correctly within the predicate.
 
• The word **no** acts as a determiner that modifies the noun phrase **small feat**, providing a more **emphatic** tone than simply saying **not a small feat**.
 
• Contextually, **climbing Mount Everest** is a monumental task, and the idiom **no small feat** perfectly captures the **gravity** and **magnitude** of such an accomplishment.
 
• Therefore, replacing the underlined part with **is no small feat** ensures both **grammatical precision** and **idiomatic naturalness**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Feat vs. Feet**:
 
 
• **Feat**: This noun refers to a **noteworthy act**, **achievement**, or **exploit** that demonstrates **bravery**, **skill**, or **strength**. It is derived from the Old French word **fait**, meaning an action or deed.
 
• **Feet**: This is the **plural form** of **foot**, referring to the anatomical part of the body or a **unit of linear measure** equal to 12 inches. Options containing **feet** are **homophonic errors** and are contextually irrelevant to the sentence.
 
 
 
• **Idiom Structure**:
 
 
• The construction **no small + [noun]** is a common rhetorical device used to indicate that something is **important** or **substantial**.
 
• Other similar expressions include **no small task**, **no small wonder**, or **no small measure**, all of which use **no** to emphasize the **size** or **intensity** of the subject.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions based on the passage:

What does a curriculum primarily prescribe?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The passage explicitly states in the first sentence that a **curriculum** is usually a **prescribed course of study** that schools are expected to follow.
 
• It serves as a framework that covers the **content** to be taught and recommends **teaching methods** to achieve specific educational objectives.
 
• The curriculum directs **what** should be taught, **how** it should be taught, and what the **learners** should expect from their education.
 
• While the curriculum provides the blueprint, the **school** serves as the actual site for its **implementation** and student **engagement**.

Therefore, the correct answer is **A course of study**.

 

**Summary:** *"A **curriculum** primarily prescribes a **course of study**, encompassing the **content** and **methodologies** required for academic instruction in schools."*

 

**Additional Information__**

 
• **Student assessment methods:** Although curricula may include guidelines for assessment, the passage focuses on the **course of study** as the primary prescribed element.
 
• **Teacher recruitment policies:** These are **administrative** or **managerial** functions of an educational institution and are not part of the academic curriculum.
 
• **Classroom seating arrangements:** This refers to **classroom management** and physical environment, which is separate from the prescribed academic **course of study**.
</ul

questions.question:
Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions based on the passage:

Which of the following best reflects the passage's implication regarding the role of schools in the implementation of curriculum?

options.text: A school is the primary setting where the objectives of a school's curriculum become actual learning experiences
Mechanical implementation of curriculum directives exists in schools, with no alteration based on student engagement or needs.
A school has no impact on how students are taught or experience a curriculum.
Schools are secondary to curriculum developers in educational outcomes and in determining how to teach.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The passage explicitly states that while curriculum makers set objectives through documents, the **school** is the **actual site** of any **curriculum implementation and engagement**.
 
• This implies that the theoretical framework provided by the **curriculum** only becomes a **real learning experience** when it is enacted within the school environment.
 
• The school is where the **dynamic interaction** happens, allowing students to **understand, question, and apply** their learning.
 
• Thus, the school is the primary setting where the **prescribed course of study** is translated into **actual learning**.

Therefore, the correct answer is **A school is the primary setting where the objectives of a school's curriculum become actual learning experiences**.

 

**Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2** is incorrect because the passage describes **curriculum engagement** as a **dynamic interaction** and an **active process**, which contradicts the idea of **mechanical implementation** without alteration.
 
• **Option 3** is incorrect because the text identifies the school as the **actual site** of implementation, meaning it has a direct and significant impact on the **educational experience**.
 
• **Option 4** is incorrect because the passage emphasizes that regardless of the **curriculum makers**, the school remains the **primary site** where learning outcomes are achieved through **student ownership** and **engagement**.
</ul
